# Why a hub for sensor-based biodiversity monitoring, and why now {.turquoise}

::: {.notes}
Nine minutes at a comfortable pace, with a minute in hand. If you are held to
seven, cut "Three bottlenecks" to its first line and give the packages slide
its three column headers only.
:::

## The sensors are already in the ground, yet the system is incomplete

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
#### Deployed, at scale, today

- **ABMS pilot (2.6.5)** – AMI traps and acoustic recorders in three habitat types across **11 countries**
- **IAS pilot (2.6.2)** – an AMI trap and a CamAlien unit in **10 countries**
- **BiodivPond pilot (2.6.8)** –acoustic recorders in **ten countries**, showing standardised pond monitoring at continental scale
- **MAMBO** and related projects – AI-based insect camera traps in **over 30 countries**
- **TABMON** – autonomous acoustic sensors across **four countries**, showing standardised passive acoustic monitoring at continental scale
:::

::: {.column}
#### Operated as independent efforts

- Ad hoc methods for annotation, verification and AI model selection, project by project
- Interoperability bottlenecks between devices, national databases and European infrastructures
- Few cross-country verified reference datasets, and those that exist are scattered and often poorly curated
- Hardware maintained country by country, needing more transnational support than expected
:::
:::

[Partners have free access to their own data – but not the tools or capacity to use it for policy-relevant insight.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
75 seconds. The point of this slide is that MANTIS asks nobody to believe in an
unproven technology. The deployments exist, the devices work, and Biodiversa+
has already paid for a good share of them. What does not exist is anything
joining them up.
:::

## Three bottlenecks – and not one of them is national

1. **Verification cannot keep up.** The volume of image and sound data has grown faster than the community's capacity to verify it, calibrate the AI models processing it, and make the outputs comparable across countries and taxa.
2. **AI accuracy is unknown outside its training context.** Moth classifiers trained on Danish and UK expert-verified images performed poorly in Slovakia, Croatia, Bulgaria and Israel. TABMON names the same annotation bottleneck as its principal constraint on scaling.
3. **Sensors still need field visits.** A substantial share of deployed acoustic recorders require manual retrieval rather than remote transfer, limiting temporal coverage and cost-efficiency.

> Left unaddressed, these problems risk automated monitoring becoming a source of fragmented, incomparable, or even unprocessed national data – repeating, at greater cost and complexity, the exact coordination problem transnational monitoring should be designed to solve.

::: {.notes}
90 seconds, and this is the slide that has to land. Model calibration, sensor
connectivity and annotation protocol design are not country-specific technical
problems, so they should not be solved redundantly across up to 27 Member
States. Read the quote out – it is the proposal's own sentence.
:::

## The aim: connective tissue

- **Connect data acquisition** – align protocols, deployments and annotations, and extend spatial and taxonomic coverage with new sensor deployments.  [Package 1]{.small}
- **Connect the data** – harmonise datasets and metadata into a seamless, quality-controlled flow from images and sounds to indicators, including transnational benchmarking of AI models.  [Package 2]{.small}
- **Connect the community** – link the users of these technologies to one another, and to the skills and resources that sustain a transnational effort.  [Package 3]{.small}

[MANTIS positions itself as a progenitor for a Thematic Hub associated with an EBOCC. Core Activity 3 primary; Core Activities 2 and 4 secondary.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
60 seconds. "Connective tissue" is the proposal's own phrase and the one image
worth repeating. MANTIS builds infrastructure for monitoring itself, not
another technology or another taxon's dataset – the feature Biodiversa+ asks of
a Task 2.5.3 activity as opposed to a conventional research grant.
:::

# What changes {.blue}

## At the end of this activity…

> …national and regional automated monitoring efforts using image and sound technologies will function as a **connected, transnational system** rather than isolated national deployments.

**Because MANTIS will have –**

- aligned data acquisition protocols and coverage across partners;
- harmonised the resulting datasets and metadata into a quality-controlled flow from raw sensor output to indicators;
- built the community, skills and self-sustaining infrastructure needed to carry this connected effort beyond the funded period.

::: {.notes}
45 seconds. The structural change in one sentence, verbatim from the proposal.
Pause after "rather than isolated national deployments" – the three clauses
under it map one-to-one onto the three packages, and onto the next slide.
:::

## Five objectives, each with a number attached {.compact}

| Objective | Target and indicator | Deadline |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **O1** Every deployment registered, in one place | 100% of active AMI, CamAlien and acoustic deployments across ≥8 partner countries, registered and machine-readable in a Camtrap DP-compliant master database | 30 Sep 2028 |
| **O2** Sensor data reaches policy without bespoke analysis | ≥4 finalised indicators live on the MANTIS dashboard, each mapped to NRR Art. 10 / EU-PoMS, the Habitats Directive, the Birds Directive or IAS Regulation 1143/2014, and auto-updating from GBIF | 30 Sep 2028 |
| **O3** Something to benchmark AI against | ≥5,000 expert-verified annotations published under FAIR principles, including ≥2,000 NewtCam annotations; ≥20% reviewed by experts from ≥2 countries | 31 Dec 2027 |
| **O4** Partners can run this themselves | 25 summer-school participants from ≥12 countries; ≥20 distinct organisations attending ≥1 of the 8 online events | 30 Jun 2028 |
| **O5** A pathway beyond Biodiversa+ | Roadmap endorsed by ≥2/3 of partners at BioMonWeek 2028, naming ≥2 concrete funding or hosting pathways | 30 Jun 2028 |

::: {.notes}
75 seconds. Do not read the table. Say: every objective carries a date and a
threshold, so at the end of the activity you can tell whether it was met
without holding a discussion about it. Point at O3 as the one everything else
depends on, and at O5 as the one that decides whether this outlives the money.
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
#### Package 1 – Scheme improvement
[Core Activity 2 · seven activities]{.small}

- Unified deployment registration system [A1.1]{.small}
- Verified datasets for transnational quality control [A1.2]{.small}
- Scaling contributions toward verification [A1.3]{.small}

:::

::: {.column}
#### Package 2 – Data flows
[Core Activity 3, primary · five activities]{.small}

- Transnational benchmarking of AI, and pipeline refinement [A2.1]{.small}
- Gold-standard implementation of media, label and annotation standards [A2.2]{.small}
- Workflows for policy-relevant indicators [A2.3]{.small}
- Scaling contributions toward transnational indicators [A2.4]{.small}
- Exemplary data-flow architecture for AMI [A2.5]{.small}
:::

::: {.column}
#### Package 3 – Capacity building
[Core Activity 4 · seven activities]{.small}

- Platform for communication and signposting [A3.1]{.small}
- MANTIS summer school [A3.2]{.small}
- Roadmap for a technical hub [A3.3]{.small}
- Technical fora and curated user guidance [A3.4]{.small}
- Two workshops on verification [A3.5]{.small}
- Four device webinars [A3.6]{.small}
- Two workshops on AI processing [A3.7]{.small}
:::
:::

[Nine deliverables and sixteen milestones, between 1 January 2027 and 30 September 2028.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
75 seconds. Do not read nineteen activity titles. Give one sentence per column:
Package 1 improves the schemes that feed the chain, Package 2 carries the data
through it, Package 3 builds the capacity that keeps it running. Then name the
three outputs a decision maker will actually look for – the registration system
online (M1.3, Aug 27), four indicators live on the dashboard (M2.2, Jul 28),
and the roadmap (D3.1, Sep 28).
:::

## Built to scale with the number of partners who join

- **CORE** – everything the two lead partners deliver regardless: registration system, verified datasets, AI benchmarking, standards, indicators, platform, summer school, roadmap. [**€314,630.80**]{.small}
- **CORE + ENHANCED** – adds the underwater acoustic pilot, the one-click AMI pipeline, technical fora, verification and AI-processing workshops, and the device webinars. [**€422,535.30**]{.small}
- **SCALABLE** – priced per participating partner: scaled contributions to verification and to indicators, sensor upgrades, and new deployments in coverage-gap countries. [**≈€54,494.36 each** – 4 person-months, 2 in-person attendances, €21,086.40 of equipment]{.small}

**Total requested: €796,850.18** – CORE + ENHANCED for the leads, plus six additional participating partners. At twelve participating partners the scalable line reaches €701,281.04.

::: {.notes}
60 seconds, and it serves two rooms at once. For Biodiversa+: the activity
descopes cleanly rather than failing – fewer partners means proportionally
fewer scaled deployments, not a thinner version of everything. For a partner
weighing whether to join: the tail of the third bullet is the commitment –
four person-months, two trips, and equipment that stays with you.

If asked: the SCALABLE tier is where the proposal's own shading and its budget
table disagree over A1.5 and A1.6, which is why this slide prices the tier by
what it funds rather than by activity ID. See MISSING-INPUTS.md. The
per-partner personnel figure is still marked TBC in section 11.1, so it is not
quoted separately here.
:::

## Sustainable past 2028

[Maintenance rests on three layers, none of which requires continued project funding.]{.lede}

1. **Permanent mandates own the outputs.** NCA CZ maintains the verified reference datasets and annotation capacity under its statutory Habitats and Birds Directive reporting duties. Aarhus University underwrites storage and curation of media in its Environmental Research Data Archive until 2031. Records and datasets are published to GBIF and Zenodo, so the data survives independently of any single host.
2. **The outputs cost nothing to keep running.** Platform, Living Protocols, standard-compliant example datasets and processing pipelines sit on GitHub Pages, with dashboards refreshed by scheduled GitHub Actions. Curation is decentralised through pull requests and moderated technical fora, so effort scales with the user community rather than with a central team.
3. **Uptake runs through schemes that continue anyway.** The registration system, benchmarking results and Camtrap DP implementations transfer to BiodivPond (2.6.8), ABMS (2.6.5) and the IAS pilot (2.6.2). Upgraded sensors are hosted at eLTER sites. Indicator workflows feed EU-PoMS and NRR Article 10 obligations that remain legally binding after 2028.

[MANTIS establishes no new operational structure. It leaves behind maintained resources and an active community of practice – and a roadmap (D3.1) offering the coordinating function to whatever vehicle carries it on, an EBOCC Thematic Hub above all.]{.small}

::: {.notes}
60 seconds. The question behind every funding decision is what happens when the
money stops. The answer here is deliberately unglamorous: no new secretariat,
no hosting bill, and outputs parked with institutions that are already legally
obliged to keep doing this.
:::

20 seconds, then questions. The likeliest three: why not leave this to the
pilots (they have no mandate or budget to work across each other); what if
fewer partners join (risk R2 – descope the scalable tier proportionally); and
what happens if verification runs late (risk R3 – a one-quarter buffer between
1.3 and 2.1, with annotation effort reallocated across partners).
:::
